chapter: Leaving New York, jazz styles and religion
title: Cutthroat jam sessions in New York
summary: New York jam sessions were everyone for himself, with players trying to out-blow each other and not helping.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Talking about this friendliness, as you call it, what was the atmosphere like in jam sessions in New York? Was that very cut-throat and competitive, too?

Well, nothin'. Just everybody for himself. Everybody and try to out-do each other and try to out-blow each other. Well, that wasn't worth a dime, you know! That's what I'm talkin' about. Musicians playing music for the musicians. A musician, he don't pay to come in to hear you play, and he don't give you nothin'. So what's the use? Ain't nothin' to it. Not a thing to it. And the guy don't want you to out-do him, and

they work against each other in them bands and whatnot, so that he won't try to help you. No! He'll be right in there trying to get your part or trying to get something... He ain't gonna try to show you how to go. No, you might find one out of a hundred that might show you some little points or something there. Every man for himself. Yeah.
